prompt: why does $.model.fork fail on resumed sessions? just tell me, don't change anything
result:
`$.model.fork` doesn't read the transcript file. It reuses the main loop's last model request in the current process: the same model, the same system prompt, the same message history. That's why it's cheap, since it's served from the prompt cache. A resumed session (`--continue`, `--resume`, `/resume`) loads its history from disk, but no request has been sent yet in this process. So on the first command after resuming there's no request to copy, and fork returns `{ isAnswered: false, reason: 'nothing-to-fork' }` instead of building one. After one normal turn, fork should work again.

**How sure this is:** the symptom is confirmed, but the cause is my inference.
- **Confirmed:** `runs/2026-10-02-handoff-model-pin/RUNLOG.md:33` records it. `claude -p --continue "/handoff"` answered `nothing-to-fork` and wrote no handoff.
- **Inferred:** the reason is my reading of how the 2.1.287 types describe fork, as quoted in `runs/2026-10-02-handoff-model-pin/PLAN.md:13`: "this session's own transcript (same model and system prompt, served from the prompt cache)". I haven't read Claude Code's source. The generated types and `docs/mods.md` in this worktree don't explain it either.

**The repo's workaround:** fall back to `$.session.messages()` plus `$.model.complete` on `$.session.model()`, with the transcript put into the prompt. This lives in `bws-kit/classify-fork.ts` (`fallbackPrompt` and the `nothing-to-fork` branch). It costs more, because there's no cache reuse and the transcript is re-sent as plain text, but it works on a resumed session's first command.

I didn't change anything.
